page_title: Mazar Marijuana Strain - Kind Green Buds

source_page_metadata.description: Explore the Mazar marijuana strain - THC levels, genetics, terpene profile, effects, flavor, and grow tips.

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-Dominant Hybrid
Genetics: Afghani × Skunk #1
Breeder: Dutch Passion
THC Content: 18–24%
CBD Content: Low (typically under 1%)
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Caryophyllene , Pinene
Primary Flavors: Earthy, Hashy, Sweet, Spicy
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to Early October
Indoor Yield: 18–22 oz per m²
Outdoor Yield: 20+ oz per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Mazar is a cultivar deeply rooted in the traditional cannabis heritage of Central Asia. Developed by Dutch Passion, the strain draws its name from Mazar-i-Sharif , a region of northern Afghanistan historically associated with some of the world’s most resin-rich cannabis plants. Afghan landrace varieties from this region have long been valued for producing dense flowers and abundant resin used in traditional hashish production .

Rather than focusing on novelty or modern flavor trends, this hybrid preserves many of the characteristics that made Afghan cannabis legendary. Heavy trichome production, robust plant structure, and deeply relaxing effects define the experience. When these landrace genetics were crossed with Skunk #1 to improve vigor and yield, the resulting plant became a powerful and reliable indica-dominant hybrid that remains widely respected among growers and enthusiasts.
Genetics and Lineage

The genetic backbone of Mazar begins with Afghan landrace cannabis originating from the mountainous regions surrounding Mazar-i-Sharif. For generations, farmers in this area cultivated plants specifically for hash production. These varieties evolved to produce thick resin layers that protect the plant from harsh environmental conditions while contributing to strong cannabinoid concentration.

Afghan landrace strains typically display compact structure, broad leaves, and dense buds that mature relatively quickly. These characteristics are clearly visible in this cultivar, which inherits the sturdy growth habits and heavy resin production associated with its Afghan ancestry. The landrace influence also contributes to the deeply relaxing physical effects that define the hybrid’s experience.

To enhance vigor and improve yield potential, breeders introduced Skunk #1 genetics into the lineage. Skunk #1 is one of the earliest stabilized cannabis hybrids and is known for its robust growth, pungent aroma, and balanced effects. Through this cross, the hybrid gained improved consistency and stronger production while maintaining its indica-dominant character.

The resulting cultivar combines the traditional qualities of Afghan cannabis with the stability of modern hybrid breeding. This balance allows growers to cultivate a plant that expresses classic indica traits while benefiting from improved performance in controlled environments.
Effects and Experience

The experience produced by Mazar tends to begin with a gentle sense of mental calm. Shortly after consumption, many individuals notice a subtle mood lift accompanied by a relaxed mental state. The early effects often feel soothing rather than stimulating.

As the experience develops, the strain’s physical qualities become more pronounced. A warm wave of relaxation gradually spreads throughout the body, loosening muscles and easing physical tension. The sensation often builds steadily rather than arriving all at once, creating a comfortable transition into deeper relaxation.

With larger doses, the experience may become deeply calming and introspective. The body often feels heavy and grounded while the mind drifts into a tranquil state. Because of this progression, many enthusiasts prefer the strain during evening hours or periods of rest when relaxation is the primary goal.
Medical Benefits

Patients exploring cannabis for therapeutic purposes frequently consider Mazar because of its strong physical effects. The deep body relaxation associated with the strain may help reduce muscular tension and chronic discomfort. Afghan-derived varieties have long been associated with physical relief due to their calming terpene and cannabinoid profiles.

Stress reduction is another potential benefit. The soothing mental qualities may help quiet racing thoughts and promote emotional balance. For individuals experiencing anxiety or mental fatigue, the calming nature of the strain can encourage a sense of ease.

Sleep support is also commonly discussed in connection with this cultivar. As the physical effects intensify, the body often settles into a deeply relaxed state that can make it easier to transition into restful sleep. Many users find this marijuana strain particularly helpful when consumed later in the evening.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The terpene profile of Mazar reflects its Afghan heritage, producing a rich and earthy aromatic experience. When the dried flower is handled, a strong scent of soil, herbs, and subtle spice typically emerges. These deep aromas are characteristic of traditional hash-producing cannabis varieties.

Myrcene contributes the earthy foundation of the fragrance, often accompanied by slightly musky undertones. Caryophyllene introduces a gentle peppery warmth that adds complexity to the scent. Limonene provides a faint citrus brightness that prevents the aroma from becoming overly heavy.

During consumption, the flavor unfolds gradually. The inhale often delivers earthy sweetness accompanied by mild herbal notes. As the vapor or smoke settles on the palate, subtle spice and woody undertones appear, leaving behind a smooth and lingering finish.
Growing Information

Cultivators often appreciate Mazar for its resilience and relatively straightforward growth characteristics. The plant typically develops a compact structure with thick stems capable of supporting heavy flowers. Its indica heritage keeps vertical growth manageable, making it well suited for indoor grows .

Indoor flowering cycles usually complete within eight to nine weeks. During this stage, the plant produces dense clusters of buds that become heavily coated with resinous trichomes. This resin production reflects the hash-producing origins of the Afghan lineage.

Outdoor cultivation can produce impressive yields when the plant is grown in climates with consistent sunlight and moderate humidity. In favorable environments, the hybrid forms thick colas that display vibrant green coloration and abundant trichome coverage. Maintaining good airflow around the buds helps ensure healthy development during the final stages of flowering.
FAQ
What kind of strain is Mazar? Mazar is an indica-dominant hybrid created by crossing Afghan landrace genetics with Skunk #1.
How strong is Mazar? THC levels typically range between 18% and 23%, providing moderate to strong potency.
What does Mazar taste like? The flavor often includes earthy sweetness, herbal notes, subtle spice, and faint citrus undertones.
Is Mazar good for sleep? Many consumers prefer it during the evening because its relaxing body effects can promote calmness and rest.
Is Mazar easy to grow? Yes. The plant is generally considered beginner-friendly due to its compact structure, resilience, and relatively short flowering time.
Final Thoughts on Mazar

Mazar stands as a tribute to the traditional cannabis genetics of Afghanistan. By combining landrace plants from the Mazar-i-Sharif region with the stability of Skunk #1, Dutch Passion created a hybrid that captures both heritage and performance.

The cultivar’s dense buds, strong resin production, and deeply relaxing effects reflect the qualities that made Afghan cannabis famous in the first place. At the same time, the addition of Skunk genetics improved yield potential and cultivation reliability. For growers and enthusiasts who appreciate classic indica varieties with historical roots, Mazar continues to represent one of the most authentic expressions of Afghan-influenced cannabis available in modern cultivation.
